blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Most taxes start from a simple formula. You take a number, you multiply by a percentage, and you have the tax. If the rate is 20% and the amount is £1,000, the tax is £200.

What changes is which number you start from. For income tax, you start from salary minus deductions. For corporate tax, you start from profit. For VAT, you start from the price of what you sell.

The formula is always the same: base amount × rate = tax. Once you see this, the subject is not mysterious. The only question is which base and which rate.

items.q: What is the simple formula for tax?
items.why: "base amount × rate = tax" — a fórmula básica da lição.

items.q: If the rate is 20% and the amount is £1,000, the tax is…
For income tax, what number do you start from?
options: The price of what you sell
items.why: "For income tax, you start from salary minus deductions."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Tax is too hard to understand.
The formula is always the same.
Only the base and the rate change.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o assunto deixa de ser misterioso — o autor discorda que seja difícil demais.

items.q: The text suggests that the three taxes are different mainly because of…
items.why: Inferência: a fórmula é a mesma; muda "which number you start from".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando o cálculo para o novo assistente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's do this together. Don't worry — it is easier than it looks. We will do three taxes, but the steps are always the same. Three steps. That's it.

Step one: find the base amount. Step two: find the rate. Step three: multiply. Base times rate equals the tax. That is the whole job.

Let's try VAT first. The price is two hundred pounds. The rate is twenty percent. So we multiply. Two hundred times zero point two is forty pounds. The VAT is forty pounds.

Now corporate tax. Here the base is not the price — it is the profit. The profit is one thousand pounds and the rate is ten percent. One thousand times zero point one is one hundred pounds.

See? Same three steps. Only the numbers change. When you know the base and the rate, the rest is just simple maths. Take your time, and always write the base down first.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many steps does Emily use?
What is step three?
items.why: "Step three: multiply. Base times rate equals the tax."

items.q: For the VAT example, how much is the tax?
Why does Emily say "only the numbers change"?
options: Because the steps stay the same for every tax
Because the rate is always twenty percent
Because VAT and corporate tax are the same tax
Because the base is always the price
items.why: Inferência: os três passos se repetem; só a base e a alíquota mudam.

items.q: How would you describe Emily's tone?
items.why: Inferência: "Don't worry… take your time" — ela é calma e encorajadora.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We always use the same formula." A formula is…
options: a fixed way to calculate something
items.why: Formula = fórmula: um jeito fixo de calcular.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "To find the tax, you ___ the base by the rate."
"The rate is twenty percent." The rate is…
Choose the correct word: "Your salary minus your ___ gives the base for income tax."
items.why: Deduction = dedução: o que se subtrai do salário.

items.q: "The base amount is the number you start from." It is…
options: the number the tax is calculated on
items.why: Base amount = base de cálculo: o número de partida.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the numbers." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's work out the tax together." To work out means to…
"Can you go over the steps again?" To go over means to…
"The new rate will roll out next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, implementar.

items.q: "Don't worry, I will walk you through it." To walk someone through means to…
items.why: Walk through = guiar passo a passo, exatamente o que Emily faz.
